findings.reason: name `reckon/crew/runs.py` as the owner and add one `run_worktree(run_id) -> Path | None` there, have the shim and mcp.py read through it, and let only the standalone guard keep a private copy with its isolation reason stated; this closes the drift the plan already saw when the read-form decision was consolidated into the shim.
findings.text: `_run_worktree(run_id)` re-derives the run's worktree from the live pointer, and two sibling copies do the same: `reckon/worker_git_shim.py:611` and `reckon/hooks/worker_git_guard.py:152`; the shim already imports `pointer_path` from `reckon/crew/runs.py` yet re-implements `read_pointer`'s body (JSON read + worktree extraction) with different missing-pointer semantics, so the pointer-reading contract now has three authorities where the owner has one

findings.reason: the guard runs as a standalone hook under a system interpreter, so a private resolver is defensible, but the plan's own §4 spine is that one rule has one authority; the comment should point at the isolation reason (the hook must not import the package) rather than an unrelated docstring, and the finding is the citation, not the duplication.
findings.text: `_config_home()` is copied into the new guard with the comment "Duplicated rather than imported — see the module docstring", but the module docstring explains only why the read-form *classifier* is imported from the shim, not why config-home resolution is re-derived; the owner is `reckon/_store.py:128` (`_config_home`), whose `RECKON_HOME`-then-`~/.config/reckon` order the guard's copy reproduces

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the fence is one deep module: `fence_argv` (`reckon/_backends.py:3013`) with `protected_paths` (:2780), `protected_read_only_binds` (:2903) and `resolved_destination` (:2859) hide bind composition, symlink resolution and write-root containment behind one composed argv at the single `launch_plan` point; the harness carry routes every file through one `seed_harness_home` (:2129), which the plan states as "one copy mechanism, not two".
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — run-pointer-to-worktree resolution is implemented three times beside the mechanism that already owns it, `reckon/crew/runs.py` (`read_pointer:575`, `pointer_path:74`, `run_dir:69`), rather than extended there once.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design cites the machinery it extends rather than inventing a parallel stack: the existing shim mechanism (`reckon/shim_lookup.py`, `reckon/host_shims/`, the new `reckon/worker_shims/git` it adds "beside the shims the worker PATH already carries"), the existing PreToolUse guard family (`reckon/hooks/native_agent_guard.py`), and the dialect sandbox flags in `reckon/_backends.py`; it selects the OS fence because the harness sandboxes (claude `--add-dir`, codex `worktree-full`) are bypassable, and states that reason.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the `git` shim (`reckon/worker_shims/git` + `reckon/worker_git_shim.py`) is a layer over git, and the plan states why the existing mechanism cannot absorb the job: a shell language cannot be parsed completely, so enforcement moves to execution time while `mutating_verb` (`reckon/worker_git_shim.py:414`) is the one classifier both the shim and the guard read.
